source.title: UFC 3-540-01: Figure B-9 Parallel Generators with Alternate Utility Supply for UPS Systems
source.note: Real public-domain drawing (US federal document), American symbol style the model never trained on; not scored, because it has no answer key yet

steps.title: Read the words
steps.plain: Read 24 pieces of text in 1.11 s. An estimator starts by reading every rating, label and note on the drawing; here the computer did it, and read again around each symbol for the small print.

steps.title: Find the symbols
steps.plain: Found 2 symbols in 0.61 s: 1 generator, 1 current transformer. Each symbol is a device the switchboard must contain, so a missed symbol is a missing line on the quotation.

steps.title: Pair labels with symbols
steps.plain: Paired 0 of 2 symbols with the label text beside them; 0 carry a rating the pricing rules can use. A breaker is priced by its amps, poles and fault rating, so the right label on the right symbol is what makes the price right.

steps.title: Read the specification and compare
steps.plain: No specification was supplied, so the board's form, protection and fault level come from the drawing notes alone (Form 4 Type 6, IP31, fault level not found). An estimator would check these against the specification before pricing.

steps.title: Pick parts and price
steps.plain: Chose 6 catalogue lines and priced the board at £7,584 (illustrative prices, 15% margin included); 3 items flagged for the estimator. Every line names the symbol, text or clause it rests on, so a reviewer can check it on the drawing.
